chapter: Berlin and the Turner and Bryant bands
title: Gene Kennedy and the Million Dollar Ballroom's Mr. Carrigan
summary: Back home he played with Gene Kennedy at the Million Dollar Ballroom on Broadway, run by mirror-lined Mr. Carrigan, with the entertainer Bennett Matthews.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: At that time, see, those girls were busy up there and I was in the band, I was busy, too. (Inaudible). And names, you know, you remember names. And so then I made this contract and I went back. And as I said, I joined --- and (sic) then I was with (inaudible) Gene Kennedy. And we started -- I was playing at the Million Dollar Ballroom, (Inaudible) Million Dollar ballroom alright. You played tangos. waltzes. on 3rd and Broadway. It was able. And the man that ran the place was named Mr. (Hugh) Carrigan. He always had his keys, and he had mirrors all around the place. You could see anything. He could see you from any angle. /And from the walls, the mirrors, if you missed a note on the trumpet, you would know. Mr. Carrigan wasn't happy. So you come out, you hear those keys. Somebody's going to go. I played with a very wonderful artist, his name was Bennett Matthews. He sang, he was (inaudible) entertainer, soprano sax, and beautiful tenor.
